questions.q: Why does parse_args() mark --store-id, --store-name, and --region as required=True?
options: It makes the script run faster
So argparse itself rejects a call missing any of them, with a usage message, before any workflow code runs
required=True is mandatory syntax with no functional effect
It lets the script accept unlimited extra arguments
questions.explain: argparse validates required arguments before the script's own logic runs, so a missing argument fails fast with a clear usage message instead of causing a confusing error deeper in the workflow.

questions.q: Which earlier lesson's exact pattern does render_config() reuse for generating the store's YAML config?
options: Lesson 9's logging setup
Lesson 13's Jinja2 Environment / FileSystemLoader pattern for generating per-environment config files
Lesson 17's webhook signature verification
Lesson 7's subprocess basics
questions.explain: render_config() loads a template with Environment(loader=FileSystemLoader(...)) and calls template.render(), the identical pattern lesson 13 used to generate per-environment nginx configs.

questions.q: In setup_store_admin(), why does the function raise a RuntimeError when result.returncode is non-zero, instead of just logging a warning and continuing?
options: RuntimeError is required syntax for any subprocess call
The next step (pulling the inventory baseline) assumes the admin account already exists, so the run needs to stop rather than continue on a broken assumption
Logging a warning would crash the Python interpreter
It has no effect either way since subprocess always succeeds
questions.explain: Continuing past a failed user-setup step would leave later steps proceeding as if setup succeeded. Raising stops the run immediately so the failure is caught by the surrounding try/except rather than compounding silently.

questions.q: Where does fetch_inventory_baseline() get the WAREHOUSE_API_TOKEN value from?
options: A hardcoded string literal in the function
An environment variable, read with os.environ["WAREHOUSE_API_TOKEN"]
The store's rendered YAML config file
A command-line argument passed to launch_store.py
questions.explain: The token is read from an environment variable rather than hardcoded or stored in the config file, following the secrets-handling rule established in the environment variables lesson.

questions.q: What does calling response.raise_for_status() accomplish after the inventory API request?
options: It retries the request automatically up to three times
It raises a Python exception if the response's HTTP status indicates an error, instead of letting a bad response be saved as if it were valid data
It converts the response into YAML format
It closes the network connection immediately
questions.explain: raise_for_status() turns an HTTP error status into a raised exception, which the surrounding try/except in main() can catch -- preventing a failed request from being saved to the baseline file as if it had succeeded.
